_notes:
Adafruit I2C STEMMA QT Rotary Encoder (product 4991): seesaw firmware on an ATSAMD09 (hardware ID 0x55) at 0x36, the default (A0-A2 jumpers give 0x37-0x3D, not claimed: a seesaw detection writes two bytes, which other chips there would take as a register and data). Seesaw registers are a module base and a function
Detection: STATUS_VERSION (0x00 0x02), 5 ms, 4 bytes: the top 16 bits are the Adafruit product number, 4991 (0x137F), the rest a date code. identPriority 1 puts it before AdafruitSoilSensor, whose detection (hardware ID 0x55) matches any SAMD09 seesaw, and AS5600 at 0x36
Init: STATUS_SWRST (0x00 0x7F = 0xFF), 20 ms; the push switch (pin 24) as an input with pull-up: GPIO DIRCLR_BULK (0x01 0x03), PULLENSET (0x01 0x0B) and BULK_SET (0x01 0x05), each with the mask 0x01000000
Poll (100 ms): ENCODER_POSITION (0x11 0x30), 5 ms, 4 bytes big-endian signed (the count since reset, one per detent); GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04), 5 ms, 4 bytes big-endian - pin 24 is bit 0 of the first byte, low when pressed. The NeoPixel (pin 6) isn't driven
Source: pins and registers from Adafruit's seesaw library and the rotary encoder examples; the version and timings checked on the bench
